chapter_theme: Sarupam, taking the Lord's form: it is reached through the eighth limb of yoga and the true path, and as everything that comes to the golden mountain takes its colour, so one who enters the guru's abode takes on the radiant form of the Lord of Kailash.

1510.reading: Abiding sarupam is the eighth limb of yoga and is not attained except in the abiding sanmarga; those who practise gain the body's attainment in its limbs, and here, as such, it is a yoga without fall.
1510.nuance: எட்டாம் யோகம் is read as samadhi, the eighth limb. அங்கத்து உடல் சித்தி may be bodily perfection or powers in the limbs; இங்கிவராக இழிவற்ற யோகமே is obscure. That sarupam needs sanmarga sits awkwardly with the scheme that gives it to yoga, unless சன்மார்க்கம் here means the true path in general.

1511.reading: As everything moving and still that comes to the golden mountain becomes that mountain's colour, so the moment one enters the abode of the guru one serves, one becomes the radiant form of the Lord of Kailash.
1511.nuance: சயிலம் (mountain) is Meru, whose gold the old image says turns all that nears it gold; the verse needs that image but names only the mountain. சாரூபம் (taking his form) is reached here through the guru, not through practice: entry into his abode (பதி) is enough.

links.note: Both make lesser things gain worth by nearness: in the Naladiyar the hare is worshipped with the moon, and the slight gain worth through friends steady as a hill; in Tirumular all that nears the golden mountain turns its colour, and the disciple takes the Lord's form.
